sources.title: Introducing Mercury 2
sources.evidence: Launch announcement names Mercury 2, explains parallel diffusion refinement, and lists tunable reasoning, 128K context, native tool use and JSON output. It announces immediate API and chat availability.

sources.title: Inception Blog
sources.evidence: The official index dates Introducing Mercury 2 to February 24, 2026. The separate Azure announcement is dated June 24, 2026.

sources.title: Models - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: The exact Mercury 2 row lists chat completions, 128K context, 50,000 maximum output tokens, tool calling, structured outputs and text format. It is separate from Mercury 2.5, Mercury 3 and Mercury Edit 2.

sources.title: List available models - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: The documented mercury-2 model object names Inception: Mercury 2, specifies context_length 128000, text input/output, and tools support. This is a documentation example, not a live authenticated endpoint check; its repeated created timestamp is not used as release evidence.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: The FAQ explicitly includes Mercury 2 among models accepting only text input and states that image generation is unsupported.

sources.title: Reasoning Efforts - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: The reasoning_effort control explicitly applies to mercury-2, with instant, low, medium and high settings; its documented default is medium.

sources.title: Mercury 2: the first reasoning model fast enough to pick up the phone
sources.evidence: This later Mercury 2 article explains the Mercury denoising model as a standard Transformer trained to predict clean text across sequence positions simultaneously. It describes Mercury 2 reasoning controls and its role as the text LLM in an ASR/LLM/TTS voice pipeline. It does not specify dense/MoE structure or parameter counts.

sources.title: Terms of Use
sources.evidence: Terms effective September 1, 2025 identify Inception AI, Inc. as owner of the services, grant restricted service-use rights and prohibit unauthorized redistribution, modification and reverse engineering. These support the descriptive proprietary license classification, not a named open-weight license.

sources.title: Mercury 2 on Azure Foundry
sources.evidence: The exact Mercury 2 deployment announcement describes a paid hourly software license separate from compute and links an Azure model card. This is a licensed deployment route, not an open-weight release.

sources.title: Mercury-2 version 1 model card - Microsoft Foundry
sources.evidence: Followed the card linked by Inception; the retrieval returned a Microsoft Foundry shell with no readable content. No technical or license claim is attributed to its unavailable body.

sources.title: Mercury: Ultra-Fast Language Models Based on Diffusion
sources.evidence: The technical report linked by Inception covers the earlier Mercury Coder Mini and Small models and Transformer denoising. It contains no Mercury 2 model specification; its earlier-model details are not transferred to Mercury 2.

sources.title: Diffusion at Scale: Introducing Mercury 3
sources.evidence: The later announcement discusses total-parameter scaling relative to Mercury 1 Mini and includes a chart labeled M2. It supplies no absolute Mercury 2 total or active parameter count and no Mercury 2 dense/MoE disclosure.

sources.title: Model Quality vs. Model Size - Mercury 3 announcement figure
sources.evidence: Visually inspected the first-party figure. M2 is explicitly labeled February 2026, but the horizontal axis gives total parameters relative to Mercury 1 Mini on a log scale. Neither an absolute count nor a numeric M2 ratio is printed. No count is inferred from chart position.

sources.title: Introducing Mercury 2.5
sources.evidence: The later release compares Mercury 2.5 with Mercury 2 on quality and deployment experience, but gives no numeric Mercury 2 parameter count, active count or expert structure. The successor's 260K context is not applied to Mercury 2.

sources.title: Research - Inception
sources.evidence: Reviewed the official research index and its Mercury technical-report link. No Mercury 2-specific technical report or model-card parameter table was found there; exact-name searches also found no first-party numeric count.

sources.title: Our Models - Inception
sources.evidence: Current model page says Mercury 2 and 2.5 are unavailable to new users, with pre-October 19 customers retaining access until November 15, 2026; enterprise support follows their agreements. This limits availability claims despite the model remaining documented.

name.note: The announcement and exact mercury-2 API identifier agree on the model name.

developer.note: Inception announces its own model; the terms identify the company as Inception AI, Inc.

family.note: The later first-party Mercury generation chart explicitly includes M2 between the first and later generations. Lowercase matches the catalog family key.

release_date.note: The official index dates the launch to February 24, and that launch announces immediate availability. June Azure distribution and later provider listings are not the original release.

open_weights.note: Official distribution is through controlled API/chat access and commercial deployments under restrictive terms. No public weight download or open-weight license was found in the reviewed primary material.

license.note: Descriptive classification supported by restricted service-use terms and the exact model's paid deployment license; this is not an SPDX or open-weight license designation.

parameters_b.note: No absolute total count found in reviewed primary sources, later releases or research. The M2 size chart is relative to an undisclosed Mercury 1 Mini count and cannot establish billions of parameters. The Azure card body was inaccessible.

active_parameters_b.note: No active count or dense/MoE structure is disclosed in the reviewed material. Do not equate active and total counts or derive either from throughput, chart position or sibling models.

architecture.note: The launch establishes diffusion generation; the later Mercury 2 explanation identifies the denoising network as a standard Transformer. Dense versus MoE, layer counts and expert configuration remain undisclosed.

context_window.note: The model table's 128K is resolved explicitly to 128000 in the exact mercury-2 documented model object. Maximum output is a separate 50000-token limit.

modalities.note: The exact model object specifies text input/output, and the FAQ expressly excludes image input for Mercury 2. Voice applications use surrounding speech components.

reasoning.note: The exact mercury-2 endpoint supports instant, low, medium and high reasoning effort, with medium documented as default.

tool_call.note: Both the Mercury 2 model table and exact model object's supported_features explicitly include tool calling.

description.value: Mercury 2 is Inception's text-only diffusion language model with adjustable reasoning, tool calling, and a 128,000-token context window.
description.note: Replaces generic purpose language with directly documented model properties and omits comparative performance claims.

patch.description: Mercury 2 is Inception's text-only diffusion language model with adjustable reasoning, tool calling, and a 128,000-token context window.
patch.notes: Diffusion generation uses a Transformer denoising network; dense/MoE details and total/active parameter counts are undisclosed in reviewed primary sources. The Mercury 3 size chart provides relative size only. As of October 26, 2026, Inception documents Mercury 2 but restricts it to existing customers until November 15, with enterprise support governed by agreements; endpoint operation was not tested.

sources.label: Exact model object and context length

summary: All 14 fields reviewed for Mercury 2. Confirmed the February 24, 2026 public release, 128000-token context, text-only modalities, reasoning and tool calling. Add proprietary licensing and the verified Transformer backbone, documenting diffusion generation separately, and replace the generic description. Total/active counts remain null: later first-party comparison material gives only relative size. Dense/MoE details and an exact-model technical report remain unavailable; the linked Azure card exposed no readable body. Current restricted-access notice is recorded without claiming endpoint testing.
